question: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in London, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Gagosian
galleries.address_hint: 6–24 Britannia Street (also 20 Grosvenor Hill and 17–19 Davies Street, Mayfair)

notes.anthropic: The largest global mega-gallery's London operation, with museum-scale exhibitions of blue-chip and estate artists since 2000.
notes.openai: A defining global mega-gallery whose London exhibitions regularly attract major institutional and market attention.

notes.anthropic: Jay Jopling's gallery defined the YBA era and remains one of Britain's most powerful dealerships, with vast Bermondsey exhibition halls.
notes.openai: London-born powerhouse with a museum-calibre programme, blue-chip roster and commanding global fair presence.

notes.anthropic: Scholarly, curator-led programme of major estates (Bourgeois, Guston) and leading living artists; a benchmark for gallery publishing and research.
notes.openai: Internationally dominant gallery combining major living artists, estates, scholarship and institutional-scale exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: London outpost of the New York powerhouse, known for historically rigorous shows and a roster spanning Doig, Ruscha and Yayoi Kusama.
notes.openai: Globally influential programme spanning canonical contemporary artists, major estates and critically prominent new work.

notes.anthropic: Global gallery with a strong technology-and-art programme and major postwar estates; a fixture of the Mayfair scene since 2012.
notes.openai: Historic international gallery representing leading postwar and contemporary artists, with exceptional institutional reach.

notes.anthropic: Founded 1967; the historic home of British conceptualism and minimalism, still central with Ai Weiwei, Anish Kapoor and Marina Abramović.
notes.openai: A foundational London gallery for conceptualism, minimalism and ambitious international contemporary practice.

notes.anthropic: Free non-collecting kunsthalle whose exhibitions, annual Pavilion commission and marathons set the international agenda for contemporary art.
notes.openai: Internationally influential public galleries commissioning major exhibitions, architecture and interdisciplinary cultural projects.

notes.anthropic: Canalside warehouse gallery with a formidable roster including Yayoi Kusama, Chris Ofili, Grayson Perry and Njideka Akunyili Crosby.
notes.openai: Highly respected programme with influential painters, photographers and installation artists and sustained museum recognition.

notes.anthropic: Since 1997 a defining London dealer, representing Urs Fischer, Sarah Lucas, Elizabeth Peyton and Jordan Wolfson.
notes.openai: Agenda-setting gallery known for rigorous exhibitions and a roster central to British and international contemporary art.

notes.anthropic: Founded 1901; the East End's landmark non-collecting institution, famed for introducing Picasso's Guernica and generations of new art to London.
notes.openai: Landmark public gallery with a long record of introducing consequential modern and contemporary artists to London.

notes.anthropic: Grand Georgian townhouse hosting museum-calibre shows of Baselitz, Kiefer, Rauschenberg and a strong younger programme.
notes.openai: Major European gallery presenting historically significant postwar figures and globally prominent contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Critically admired programme (Steve McQueen, Lynette Yiadom-Boakye, Hurvin Anderson) balancing museum-quality shows with market clout.
notes.openai: Highly regarded programme linking leading British artists with important international and moving-image practices.

notes.anthropic: Cologne/Berlin gallery whose London space champions conceptual and feminist positions: Barbara Kruger, Cindy Sherman, Rosemarie Trockel.
notes.openai: Critically rigorous international gallery representing major conceptual, feminist and media-based practices.

galleries.name: Maureen Paley
galleries.address_hint: 60 Three Colts Lane, Bethnal Green (and 21 Herald Street)

notes.anthropic: Opened 1984 in her own house; the pioneer of East End galleries and long-time dealer for Wolfgang Tillmans and Gillian Wearing.
notes.openai: Pioneering East End gallery instrumental in developing generations of critically important artists.

notes.anthropic: Since 1946 the crucible of British experimental art, film and performance; still a key early platform for emerging artists.
notes.openai: Historically vital experimental institution supporting contemporary art, film, performance and countercultural debate.

notes.anthropic: Since 1995 a globally minded roster (Yinka Shonibare, Kehinde Wiley, Mamma Andersson) with a strong fair and institutional presence.
notes.openai: Established international gallery with a strong record in painting, sculpture and artists from the African diaspora.

notes.anthropic: Influential dealer of internationally acclaimed artists including Tala Madani, Rirkrit Tiravanija and Sophie von Hellermann.
notes.openai: Influential programme of internationally recognised artists, particularly strong in painting and conceptually driven installation.

notes.anthropic: Commissioning space with an unrivalled record of first solo shows by artists who later win the Turner Prize.
notes.openai: One of London's most respected commissioning institutions, frequently backing artists before wider international recognition.

galleries.name: Modern Art
galleries.address_hint: 4–8 Helmet Row, EC1 (also 7 Bury Street, St James's)

notes.anthropic: Stuart Shave's gallery, a consistently sharp barometer of contemporary painting and sculpture since 1998.
notes.openai: Stuart Shave's influential gallery supports prominent international artists with a distinctive, critically followed programme.

notes.anthropic: Beloved non-collecting space known for launching international artists into UK institutional recognition, plus ceramics and residencies.
notes.openai: Leading public gallery known for artist development, thoughtful commissions and influential first London presentations.

notes.anthropic: Historic Victorian gallery reinvented as a leading commissioning venue with strong community and education programmes.
notes.openai: Major public gallery combining ambitious commissions, emerging-artists programmes and sustained local engagement.

notes.anthropic: Critically respected gallery representing Nicole Eisenman, Michael Dean and Cornelia Baltes; a mainstay of the East End since 2005.
notes.openai: Critically admired gallery with an influential intergenerational roster and strong international fair presence.

notes.anthropic: Stewards key estates (Robert Mapplethorpe, Lygia Clark, Birgit Jürgenssen) alongside a strong contemporary roster.
notes.openai: Critically distinguished gallery combining influential contemporary artists with major rediscovered artists and estates.

notes.anthropic: Milanese gallery's London home in a Grade II listed townhouse, showing Cattelan, Yan Pei-Ming and leading Italian positions.

notes.anthropic: Historic South African gallery whose London space is a leading platform for African and diaspora artists including William Kentridge.
notes.openai: Landmark African-founded gallery with a politically engaged roster and deep international institutional influence.

notes.anthropic: Vanguard gallery that launched Oscar Murillo, Ed Atkins and Issy Wood; hugely influential on younger London taste.

notes.anthropic: Above-the-pub gallery since 1997 with a curatorially adventurous programme and consistent international fair presence.
notes.openai: Enduring East End gallery celebrated for discovering artists and maintaining an adventurous international programme.

notes.anthropic: Jane Hamlyn's gallery, home to Cornelia Parker, Tacita Dean, Fiona Tan and Bridget Smith since 1989.
notes.openai: Durable, critically respected gallery especially strong in conceptual, installation and moving-image practices.

notes.anthropic: Transatlantic gallery with a refined programme of painting, from Alex Katz to Antonio Calderara and Honor Titus.
notes.openai: Longstanding London gallery balancing major postwar figures with established and emerging contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Since 2002 a tastemaking East End gallery showing Goshka Macuga, Francis Upritchard and Matt Stokes.
notes.openai: Highly regarded independent gallery with a focused, institutionally successful roster and strong curatorial credibility.

notes.anthropic: International residency programme and gallery giving many artists their first UK institutional show.
notes.openai: Internationally connected nonprofit whose residencies and exhibitions have launched many consequential artistic careers.

notes.anthropic: Cornelia Grassi's quietly authoritative gallery representing Tomma Abts, Jennifer Packer and Aliza Nisenbaum.
notes.openai: Low-key but deeply respected gallery representing artists with substantial critical and institutional standing.

notes.anthropic: One of the most watched younger galleries, with acclaimed international artists and standout Basel and Frieze presentations.
notes.openai: Critically prominent gallery supporting experimental emerging and mid-career artists with growing institutional visibility.

notes.anthropic: Artist studios plus a former chapel gallery known for ambitious commissions and long-overdue rediscoveries.

notes.anthropic: Tommaso Corvi-Mora's long-running programme, key to the careers of Roger Hiorns, Rachel Feinstein and Liz Larner in the UK.
notes.openai: Longstanding independent gallery known for distinctive artists and sustained critical credibility.

notes.anthropic: International gallery bridging modern estates and market-leading contemporary painters across its London space.
notes.openai: International gallery with significant market influence across contemporary painting and established postwar art.

notes.anthropic: Blue-chip specialist in 1980s–90s American art — Prince, Sherman, Condo — with museum-quality secondary market shows.
notes.openai: Blue-chip gallery mounting focused exhibitions of major postwar and contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Andrew Wheatley and Martin McGeown's fiercely independent gallery, historically important for Lucy McKenzie, Marc Camille Chaimowicz and Ed Atkins.
notes.openai: Idiosyncratic, architecturally distinctive gallery with a long-standing reputation for demanding conceptual programmes.

notes.anthropic: Long-running gallery with a notably strong roster of women artists and an active fair and publishing programme.
notes.openai: Established gallery with a closely watched programme of international painters and interdisciplinary artists.

notes.anthropic: Politically engaged programme including Lubaina Himid and Andrea Büttner; several Turner Prize winners among its artists.

notes.anthropic: Paris-based global gallery whose London space brings Murakami, Kusama editions and pop-inflected international names.
notes.openai: Globally prominent gallery whose London branch extends a high-profile international programme and market network.

notes.anthropic: Free exhibition centre in restored Georgian silk-merchant houses, celebrated for rigorous historical and archival exhibitions.
notes.openai: Independent nonprofit respected for scholarly, unconventional exhibitions and reassessments of overlooked practices.

notes.anthropic: Grew from a Peckham project space into an influential dealer of post-internet and feminist practices, publishing critical texts.
notes.openai: Influential gallery emerging from artist-led culture, known for politically incisive and digitally informed practices.

notes.anthropic: Robin Klassnik's legendary production-led space since 1979, famous for major commissions by Willie Doherty and Mike Nelson.
notes.openai: Seminal artist-centred organisation with a decades-long history of enabling ambitious installations and new work.

notes.anthropic: Sharp emerging-artist programme with consistent presence at Liste and other discovery-driven fairs.
notes.openai: Respected emerging gallery with a strong record of developing experimental artists and international partnerships.

notes.anthropic: Pioneering platform for technologically and politically charged practices, including DIS, Juliana Huxtable and Rachel Rose.

notes.anthropic: Since 1992 a champion of underrecognised figures such as Frank Bowling and Hew Locke, with a New York outpost.
notes.openai: Established gallery with deep roots in East London and a respected transatlantic, intergenerational programme.

notes.anthropic: Cork Street institution since 1957, dealing in postwar modern masters alongside contemporary sculpture.
notes.openai: Major longstanding dealer in modern and contemporary art with strong scholarship and blue-chip fair presence.

notes.anthropic: Recovers overlooked feminist, conceptual and performance practices; a research-heavy programme with strong institutional placements.
notes.openai: Known for feminist, conceptual and performance art, including important historical reassessments and estates.

notes.anthropic: Distinguished gallery for constructivism and its legacies, representing David Hockney's prints, Anthony Caro and Yuko Shiraishi.
notes.openai: Historically important London gallery with enduring strengths in abstraction, constructivism and contemporary art.

notes.anthropic: Fitzrovia gallery with a strong transatlantic painting programme and steady art-fair visibility.
notes.openai: Established independent gallery with a distinctive international roster and consistent institutional placements.

notes.anthropic: Brutalist non-collecting gallery whose ambitious survey exhibitions have shaped British understanding of contemporary art since 1968.
Ambitious mid-size gallery known for socially engaged and research-based practices from across the globe.
notes.openai: Research-oriented programme engaging politics, technology, ecology and global contemporary practice.

notes.anthropic: Legendary dealer of conceptual and film-based artists — Gerhard Richter, Steve McQueen, Tacita Dean, William Kentridge.

notes.openai: Leading European gallery with a formidable roster across painting, sculpture and conceptually ambitious practice.
Historically important gallery renowned for postwar European art and intellectually demanding contemporary painting.
